messages:
Maya: FYI team — saw Northbridge onboarding traffic this morning and p95 token latency jumped ~220ms for 30m during 09:05-09:35 UTC. Their renewal call is next week, want to be proactive.
Maya: Proposed mitigation: 1) enable int8 quant profile for their model, 2) swap traffic to redwood/compact-v2 as a canary, 3) split routing 80% Dedicated pool / 20% Hosted for safety.
Ravi: Can you paste the invocation pattern? e.g., prompt lengths, streaming vs non-streaming, embedding mix?
Maya: Most calls are non-streaming chat completions, median prompt ~180 tokens, responses ~120 tokens. Minimal embeddings. Spike correlates with morning batch of marketing generation jobs.
Jordan: If we do int8 on their dedicated pool we need to check kv-cache mem pressure. Can you share recent runtime traces?
Maya: Pasting sanitized trace snippet from today (09:10 UTC):
```
[09:10:03] req_id=abcd1234 model=redwood/full-v1 seq_in=178 seq_out=126 batch=1 device=gpu-0 p95=540ms
[09:10:04] req_id=efgh5678 model=redwood/full-v1 seq_in=182 seq_out=130 batch=4 device=gpu-0 p95=870ms
```
Maya: Notice the batched requests (batch=4) had the worst p95.
Ravi: That suggests batching heuristics plus attention kernel thresholds are tripping. Compact-v2 typically reduces per-token compute ~30-40% for these seq lengths. int8 can cut memory bandwidth too.
Ravi: Suggest canary plan: start with 10% traffic to compact-v2 quant-int8 on dedicated, monitor p95 and error rate for 2h, then step to 50% if stable.
Jordan: +1. Also set autoscale headroom to 25% for that pool during canary and enable KV-prefetch TTL=60s to avoid cache thrash.
Maya: Draft config snippet for the canary route:
```
route: northbridge-canary
- match: customer_id == "northbridge"
- weight: 10
- model: redwood/compact-v2:int8
- pool: dedicated-nb-2
- autoscale_headroom: 0.25
```
Maya: I'll schedule an enablement call with Lena to walk through the change and capture any internal QA concerns. Lena, are you available today 16:00 UTC?
Lena (Northbridge): Hi all — yes 16:00 UTC works. We did notice timeout errors in their UI during the spike (mostly client-side 10s timeouts). Any risk of regenerated outputs changing semantics with compact model?
Ravi: Good question. Compact-v2 has the same tokenization and top-level behaviors; differences are mostly in subtle output phrasing. We'll add a small evaluation set (10 representative prompts) and run regression checks pre-swap.
Maya: I'll prepare the eval set. Also proposing a rollback policy: if p95 > baseline + 150ms or error_rate > 0.5% for 15m, automatically revert routing to full-v1. ops-bot, can you create that alert?
ops-bot: Alert created: northbridge-canary-p95; threshold=baseline+150ms; eval_window=15m; action=route_revert_to:redwood/full-v1
Ravi: One more ops note — during the 09:10 spike batch=4 looks like continuous batching overflowed GPU queue. Consider adjusting continuous_batch_size_limit for dedicated pool from 64 -> 48 for the canary window.
Jordan: I'll pre-provision an extra 1 GPU to the dedicated pool for the canary start window (09:50-12:00 UTC) and watch queue latency.
Maya: Plan agreed. Action items: 1) Maya prepare eval prompts + schedule 16:00 call with Lena, 2) Ravi & Jordan deploy canary routing and set autoscale/headroom + batch limit, 3) ops-bot monitor and auto-revert alert.
Lena (Northbridge): Thanks — appreciate the proactive approach. If the canary looks good we are happy to keep the compact path long-term to save on costs.
Maya: Awesome. Will post results in this thread after the 2h canary. :thumbsup:
